title: Conditional Long ADBE — Management Vacuum Discount, Strong AI Fundamentals Intact
entry: CONDITIONAL — Do NOT enter on June 12 (management uncertainty is maximum on Day 1 of the CFO departure announcement). Entry fires only when ONE of the following conditions is confirmed: (1) CFO replacement named or interim appointment announced, OR (2) Two consecutive sessions stabilizing above $200 with no further C-suite departure news. Entry zone $200-215. Do not chase above $220 before the management signal is confirmed — the morning briefing's Don't Buy designation holds until management stability is demonstrated. The prior conditional long (long-adbe-post-earnings-ai-monetization-2026-06-11) was thesis-broken when the CFO departure prevented the gap-up entry; this opportunity targets the distressed valuation level after the management discount has been priced.
stop_loss: $190 daily close (~6.4% below entry midpoint $207.50) — implies the AI-substitution bear thesis is validated by further fundamental deterioration beyond the management vacuum, OR additional C-suite departures create a full leadership crisis
targets: $240 — CFO replacement named; institutional confidence returns; ADBE recovers to the prior conditional-entry zone; Q2 AI ARR data fully digested; +15.7% from entry midpoint $207.50
$265 — Management stability confirmed over 4+ weeks; Firefly AI ARR continues sequential acceleration in mid-quarter commentary; Adobe reaffirms FY2026 revenue guidance above $25.6B; +27.7%

$295 — Full recovery from the -30%+ YTD discount as the AI-substitution bear thesis is systematically unwound; enterprise renewal cycle intact; ADBE approaches Q1 2026 analyst consensus price target zone; +42.2%
catalyst: Adobe Q2 FY2026 results reported June 11 AH: non-GAAP EPS $5.96 (beat $5.81 consensus), Firefly AI ARR tripled year-over-year — the core AI-monetization thesis is empirically validated. However, CFO Dan Durn simultaneously announced departure to Marvell effective June 15, creating a dual C-suite vacancy (CFO departing + CEO search ongoing). Stock traded June 12 in the range $203.35-$234.07 with shares at $208.98 — the management instability discount is now priced. This is the setup to monitor for a distressed entry once the management uncertainty peak passes: fundamentals proved, valuation compressed.
thesis:
ADBE at $208-215 is pricing two independent risks simultaneously: (1) the AI-substitution bear thesis (generative AI cannibalizing Photoshop) and (2) the management vacuum (dual C-suite absence). The Q2 FY2026 beat empirically refutes risk (1) — EPS $5.96 vs $5.81, Firefly AI ARR tripled sequentially, and Digital Media ARR growth confirms enterprise subscriptions are growing alongside AI competition. Risk (2) is real but temporary: CFO replacement timelines for large-cap tech companies average 45-90 days, and Adobe's $25B buyback authorization, clean balance sheet, and operational continuity mean the business does not require heroic CFO action in the near term. The conditional entry structure ensures we don't initiate until the management uncertainty peak has passed.

The distressed entry thesis is straightforward: the AI-monetization case is now empirically confirmed by actual revenue data, the management uncertainty will be resolved within 60-90 days, and the stock at $208 is pricing a permanent 12-15% discount to the pre-CFO-announcement level — a discount that should close as management stability is demonstrated. Historical comparables for CFO-departure events at large-cap software companies (Salesforce 2024, ServiceNow 2023) created 8-12% short-term discounts that fully recovered within 6-10 weeks once replacements were made. ADBE's deeper -30%+ YTD discount (predating today's news) means the management vacuum is being layered on top of an already-discounted valuation, creating a compounded margin of safety on the fundamental thesis.

The macro overlay is mildly constructive: VIX at 19.44 reflects STEP ASIDE territory (not full risk-off), and ADBE's enterprise-software subscription model is not highly sensitive to short-term rate moves. FOMC June 16-17 is a risk (Warsh hawkish bias), but ADBE's SaaS model doesn't rely on rate-sensitive consumer demand. The primary incremental risk is execution: if Firefly AI ARR growth decelerates in Q3 FY2026 (reported September), the management vacuum gets compounded onto a fundamental deterioration story. The $190 stop captures this scenario before it can develop.

The counter-party is the ADBE bear who argues: (1) the CFO departure signals a deeper company-culture or strategy problem not visible externally — what does Durn know that the market doesn't; (2) the $25B buyback is window-dressing for a business losing pricing power to generative AI; (3) even if Firefly ARR is growing, the total ARR growth trajectory is insufficient to justify a $95B+ market cap for a company growing 10-13% annually. The $190 stop enforces discipline: if these bear arguments are correct, the stop is triggered within weeks of entry.
bull_case: New CFO named within 30 days (internal promotion or external candidate known to be in process); stock gaps 8-12% higher on announcement. Q3 FY2026 preliminary data confirms Firefly AI ARR sequential acceleration sustained. ADBE recovers toward $240-265 as management discount closes and AI-monetization re-rating resumes. Potential M&A interest if stock lingers below $220.
bear_case: CFO replacement process takes 90+ days with multiple failed candidates; CEO search remains unresolved; both vacancies create an operational leadership vacuum delaying critical AI product decisions. Additional executive or key product manager departures widen the leadership crisis. ADBE falls below $190; stop triggered. Tail: hostile takeover bid at $175-200 validates the bear case by confirming the business is worth less than management's projections.
invalidation: $190 daily close, OR second C-suite departure announced (CTO, CPO) widening the leadership vacuum, OR Q3 FY2026 preliminary Digital Media ARR data shows YoY growth below 8% confirming AI-substitution, OR entry condition remains unmet for 60+ calendar days (staleness closure)

outcome.note: ADBE gapped to ~$168 pre-market June 15 (morning briefing est.), well below the $190 daily-close stop. Entry conditions had been met via two consecutive closes above $200 (June 13-14) with no additional C-suite departures, but a new wave of selling — likely freemium model concerns layered on the CFO departure — drove through the stop before the session opened. Effective exit at ~$175 on gap-fill; actual fill likely between $168 and $185.
